scope: Source-demonstration coverage for ranks 5,6,8 plus all ten actual C# Demo outputs; numerical-only scope as explicitly approved.
status: Tests implemented; execution and final numerical gates are recorded separately.

cases.demonstration: Random fruit/basket initialization at grid_size=10.
assertions: Original exclusive randint bounds and initialized state are checked.
All seeded resets feed a verified 1,000-episode numerical loop.
limits: Mixed scalar/size-one-array np.asarray in the old source is repaired using explicit scalar extraction.

cases.demonstration: Catch observations, action transitions, game-over rewards using the original 10x10 grid and 1,000-episode count.
assertions: All 9,000 action/state/reward rows compared byte-for-byte to NumPy.
Fixed-Q fixture wins exactly 330 of 1,000 episodes; every observation shape is (1,100).
limits: The fixed-Q predictor is a declared test fixture, not a trained Keras network or a reproduced learning-success claim.

cases.demonstration: epsilon=.1 random versus first-argmax action selection.
assertions: Exact seeded action sequence; epsilon endpoints and first-index ties; invalid epsilon rejected.

cases.demonstration: Capacity 500, sampled batch 50 and per-action Bellman targets.
assertions: Memory eviction and original random sampling path exercised, not only injected indices.
Every sampled input and target agrees with NumPy; terminal/no-bootstrap and unselected action targets checked.
Stored state survives disposal of the caller's step scope.

cases.demonstration: Neural-network fitting, epoch loss, trained win count, model serialization.
cases.reason: Outside the explicitly approved numerical-only scope. No Keras training or checkpoint results are represented as verified.

cases.demonstration: Load a trained model, play ten games and save numbered frames.
cases.reason: Requires the trained Keras model and graphics/file IO; numerical environment and argmax behavior are covered separately.

cases.demonstration: Seed zero, population 50, sigma .1, alpha .001, target [.5,.1,-.3], all 300 updates.
assertions: All 301 parameter vectors and rewards are compared, not just the final point.
Existing final-weight byte gate remains in force.
limits: A stochastic optimizer need not improve monotonically; the displayed final reward can be worse than checkpoint 280.

cases.demonstration: Printed weights and reward before update 0.
assertions: All three weights agree at the source's 8 printed decimals; reward at 6 printed decimals.
The full underlying state/reward trace is also compared with a live NumPy run.
limits: Printed precision is not a byte-precision claim for rounded source text.
